title: A CXL Memory Rack for Multi-Turn LLM Serving
event_hint: HyMCache: a CXL memory rack for multi-turn LLM serving built from cost-efficient CXL-hybrid memory (CXL-HM: small in-device DRAM + large SSD-backed capacity behind a CXL interface), using request-level prefix prefetching and opportunistic write buffering to stage latency-critical KV reads in device DRAM; evaluated on a real CXL-HM prototype under single-aggregator and PD-disaggregated serving.
problem: Long-context, multi-turn, and agentic LLM workloads increasingly reuse previously processed context, so KV-cache reuse is essential to cut redundant computation. But this reuse shifts the bottleneck to the memory tier that stores and serves reusable KV states at cluster scale: GPU HBM and host DRAM are too costly to scale to TB-scale shared context capacity, motivating remote tiers built from lower-cost, higher-capacity media. Conventional CMM-H devices treat internal DRAM as a transparent LRU cache, which mis-handles multi-turn KV access: LRU-induced refills let one-shot-wonder blocks occupy space that should hold upcoming prefix blocks, and dirty evictions interleave backend writebacks with read traffic, degrading effective read bandwidth.
mechanism: HyMCache uses CXL-HM (small in-device DRAM + large SSD-backed capacity behind a CXL interface) as an explicitly managed staging space for KV objects rather than a transparent LRU cache. It exploits the read-dominant, predictable, append-only nature of multi-turn KV-cache access. Two design points: (1) KV-object prefetching — multi-turn prefix-cache lookup reveals the ordered list of KV objects an inference request will consume, and the serving runtime passes this object-level access order to CXL-HM via an explicit prefetch interface so upcoming KV objects are staged in device DRAM before foreground remote reads arrive; (2) latency-hiding staging window with opportunistic write buffering for newly generated KV. LLM workers access the remote KV tier as remote memory through RDMA (prototype path) or a CXL switch-based fabric; the remote tier is exposed as a unified memory address space backed by one or more CXL-HM devices. A read is served directly from internal DRAM if the KV object is already staged, otherwise the object is first copied from SSD-backed capacity into internal DRAM before being returned.

evidence.claim: Headline serving comparison (abstract): on a real CXL-HM prototype under both single-aggregator and PD-disaggregated serving, under the same DRAM budget HyMCache outperforms local LMCache by 3.0x in single-node serving and 1.45x in PD-disaggregated serving. Compared with 1 TB distributed-DRAM Mooncake, HyMCache incurs about 30% lower performance but uses 16x less DRAM. (Reported as abstract headline; the visible Evidence Pack exposes the prefetching microbenchmark and LMSYS Turn-6 latency CDF but not the full per-config comparison table behind the 3.0x/1.45x/-30% ratios.)
evidence.value: 3.0x vs local LMCache (single-node); 1.45x vs local LMCache (PD-disaggregated); ~30% lower vs 1TB Mooncake at 16x less DRAM
evidence.condition: same DRAM budget; real CXL-HM prototype; single-aggregator and PD-disaggregated serving

evidence.claim: Prefetching microbenchmark (Figure 13a): on heavy random-read requests to the remote CXL-HM tier managed by HyMCache, enabling prefetching improves performance by 37% vs prefetch-off.
evidence.condition: heavy random-read microbenchmark against remote CXL-HM tier

evidence.claim: LMSYS read-heavy serving, Turn 6, external cache hit rate >90% (512 conversations, concurrency 64, input >2K chars): HyMCache prefetching raises average and peak remote KV loading bandwidth (Figure 13b) and reduces end-to-end median/p99 latency (Figure 13c) vs prefetch-off; latency CDF at Turn 6 (Figure 12b) shows HyMCache maintains a similar latency distribution to LMCache/Redis despite relying on remote SSD-backed CXL-HM capacity, by preserving reusable prefix KV blocks in the remote tier.
evidence.value: external cache hit >90% at Turn 6; prefetch raises KV-load BW and lowers E2E median/p99 latency; CDF matches LMCache/Redis
evidence.baseline: HyMCache prefetch-off; LMCache + Redis (memory-backed local/remote cache)
evidence.condition: LMSYS dataset, 512 conversations, concurrency 64, input >2K chars, Turn 6

evidence.claim: Workload motivation (Section 3): multi-turn KV-cache access is read-dominant, predictable, and append-only; conventional CMM-H LRU management mis-handles it — LRU refills leave one-shot-wonder blocks occupying space needed for upcoming prefix blocks, and dirty evictions interleave backend writebacks with reads, degrading effective read bandwidth. This motivates treating CXL-HM internal DRAM as an explicitly managed staging space rather than a transparent cache.
evidence.value: multi-turn KV access is read-dominant/predictable/append-only; LRU + dirty eviction degrade CMM-H read bandwidth
evidence.condition: multi-turn LLM serving KV-cache access pattern analysis

evidence.claim: Prototype access path: LLM workers access the remote KV tier as remote memory through RDMA (example path in the prototype) or a CXL switch-based fabric; the remote tier is a unified memory address space backed by one or more CXL-HM devices. Reads are served from internal DRAM if the KV object is already staged, otherwise copied from SSD-backed capacity into internal DRAM before being returned.
evidence.value: RDMA or CXL-switch fabric; unified address space over >=1 CXL-HM devices; staged-read or SSD-fill-then-read
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 6 (Section 3.3 LLM Targeted CXL-HM, Figure 6)

evaluation_context: Hardware: a real CXL-HM prototype (CXL-hybrid memory: small in-device DRAM + large SSD-backed capacity behind a CXL interface); remote KV tier accessed as remote memory via RDMA (prototype example path) or CXL switch-based fabric; one or more CXL-HM devices forming a unified address space. Serving configs: single-aggregator (single-node) and PD-disaggregated. Baselines: local LMCache (same DRAM budget) and 1 TB distributed-DRAM Mooncake. Workloads: heavy random-read microbenchmark against the remote CXL-HM tier; LMSYS dataset (512 conversations, concurrency 64, input >2K chars, Turn 6, external cache hit rate >90%). Compared systems also include Redis (memory-backed local/remote cache combination). Headline ratios (3.0x / 1.45x / -30% vs Mooncake at 16x less DRAM / +37% prefetch) are reported in the abstract/conclusion and supported by the LMSYS/prefetch figures; the full per-config comparison table is not in the visible Evidence Pack.
limitations: The headline 3.0x (single-node) / 1.45x (PD-disaggregated) vs local LMCache and the ~30%-lower-vs-Mooncake-at-16x-less-DRAM figures are reported in the abstract and conclusion, but the visible Evidence Pack exposes only the prefetching microbenchmark (+37%) and the LMSYS Turn-6 latency CDF/bandwidth figures; the detailed per-config comparison table (absolute throughput, latency, and the exact DRAM budgets of HyMCache vs LMCache vs Mooncake) is not in the visible evidence, so the headline ratios are currently claims whose precise conditions should be verified. The prototype uses RDMA as the example access path; CXL switch-fabric results are described but their separate measurements are not in the visible evidence. Absolute SSD/device-DRAM capacities, the CXL-HM device count, and whether the SSD-backed tier is TLC/QLC are not pinned in the visible evidence. Single-prototype scope; no multi-rack or failure-mode evaluation is visible. PD-disaggregated serving baseline identity (beyond 'local LMCache') and the exact Mooncake configuration (1 TB distributed DRAM) are given only at headline granularity.
project_relevance: Relevant to the cross-region / Agent-Cache card's question of how to store, move, and reuse KV-cache (and by extension reusable agent context) at cluster scale using lower-cost, higher-capacity media: HyMCache is a concrete CXL-HM rack that treats device DRAM as an explicitly managed staging space for predictable, append-only multi-turn KV access, using request-level prefix prefetching to hide SSD latency. The 16x-DRAM-reduction vs Mooncake at ~30% performance cost is a directly relevant cost/capacity tradeoff point for TB-scale shared context. The prefetching design (object-level access order revealed by prefix-cache lookup, passed to the device) is a concrete instance of the card's 'prefetch and placement to reduce latency' lever. Caveat: the headline ratios need the full comparison table before a deployable magnitude claim; the result is single-turn-reuse KV rather than WAN cross-region, so it speaks to shared-tier capacity more than to WAN RTT tradeoffs.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the absolute per-config throughput, latency, and DRAM budgets behind the 3.0x (single-node) and 1.45x (PD-disaggregated) vs local LMCache and the ~30%-lower-vs-Mooncake-at-16x-less-DRAM headline ratios?
